newsitem.title: INDIA: U.S.'s AMD to sell new processor by March.
newsitem.headline: U.S.'s AMD to sell new processor by March.

text.p: Advanced Micro Devices Inc (AMD) of the United States said on Tuesday it will start world-wide marketing of its advanced AMD-K6 micro processor by the end of March.
Vijar Parmar, regional marketing manager for Advanced Micro Devices Far East Ltd, said it had begun shipping initial samples of the AMD-K6 to development partners.
Advanced Micro Devices Far East Ltd is a wholly-owned subsidiary of U.S. micro processor maker AMD.

"The company has commenced sampling of its sixth-generation AMD-K6 processor to key development partners," Parmar told a news conference in the Indian capital, saying the AMD-K6 had a performance level equivalent to that of Intel's Pentium Pro processor.
"We will start marketing the product anytime in the first quarter of 1997," he said.
Parmar said the company currently controls about 12 percent of world micro processor sales. "Our target is to increase the share to 15 percent by 1998," he said.
